articles.title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA unveil Vera Rubin AI systems and new sovereign cloud tools
articles.description: New A5X computing instances are scheduled for November 2026, alongside expanded support for open AI models, confidential computing and locally controlled AI deployments Google Cloud and NVIDIA have announced new GPU-powered computing systems, sovereign AI capabilities and security tools designed to support increasingly complex enterprise AI workloads. Unveiled at NVIDIA GTC Berlin the updates include Google Cloud's forthcoming A5X bare-metal instances, powered by NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, with general availability expected in November. The companies are also introducing additional options for organizations that need to operate AI models within specific geographic jurisdictions or isolated computing environments, including new capabilities for Google Distributed Cloud and the public cloud. The changes span computing hardware, networking, storage, model deployment and data protection, as Google Cloud develops infrastructure for agentic AI systems capable of carrying out multi-step tasks. Vera Rubin infrastructure targets larger AI workloads Google Cloud's A5X instances will bring NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform into its AI Hypercomputer infrastructure, combining GPU acceleration with networking and storage technologies designed for large-scale model training and inference. The company says the new systems will be available in additional regions across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA), supporting organizations with regional data residency and sovereignty requirements. A central component is Google's Virgo Network, which the company says will support clusters of up to 80,000 Rubin GPUs at a single site and as many as 960,000 GPUs across multiple sites. These figures describe the infrastructure's intended scaling capacity rather than an announced operational deployment. Other updates include support for NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage through Google Cloud Managed Lustre, allowing data to move directly into GPU memory, and advanced caching designed to manage longer AI interactions while reducing repeated processing. Google Kubernetes Engine will also support workload orchestration on A5X instances, including resource scheduling and network management for distributed AI systems. Stephan Pretorius, Chief Technology Officer at WPP, points to the potential application of the infrastructure in creative production. “With Google Cloud’s A5X instances accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, our WPP Creative and Production teams can direct intelligent agents that perform frame-accurate quality checks and adapt brand assets seamlessly.” Google introduces new sovereign AI and local Gemini deployment options Beyond computing capacity, the partnership introduces new options for organizations seeking greater control over where AI systems operate and how their data is processed. Google Cloud is adding support for open-weight models including Gemma, Mistral and NVIDIA Nemotron to its Sovereign Cloud portfolio, allowing organizations to retain custody of model weights and runtime environments. The company has also made NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs generally available through Google Distributed Cloud, using NVIDIA HGX B300 systems for computing deployments within an organization's own facilities. Gemini 3.5 Flash is being added to these isolated environments, enabling multimodal AI processing involving text, audio, images and video without requiring workloads to operate outside the local infrastructure. Another addition is enterprise search powered by Gemini and multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Available in preview for air-gapped Google Distributed Cloud deployments, the technology is designed to let organizations search, summarize and examine internal documents, media and other information while keeping processing inside their controlled environment. Google is also extending support for NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and Nemotron 3.5 SuperVL on its Gemini platform, including tools for model customization and simulated environments used in robotics and autonomous vehicle development. Confidential computing protections extend across Google Cloud The companies have also introduced security updates intended to protect sensitive information while AI models are being trained or used. Google Cloud's Confidential G4 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, are now generally available. Confidential computing is also available on A4 instances using NVIDIA HGX B200 hardware and Intel TDX. A further development is Confidential Bare Metal on A4X Max instances, which use NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 technology and hardware-based security measures to protect AI models, intellectual property and user prompts during processing. These capabilities are aimed at organizations managing sensitive AI workloads, particularly where data protection, local operational control and infrastructure isolation are requirements. The announcements cover technologies at different stages of availability. Confidential G4 instances and Blackwell Ultra GPUs on Google Distributed Cloud are generally available, while the new enterprise search capability remains in preview. Google Cloud's Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances are scheduled to become generally available in November 2026, including in additional EMEA regions. articles.title: GTN and AmInvestment Bank expand market access for Malaysian investors
articles.description: SINGAPORE, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GTN, the global fintech powering limitless investment, and AmInvestment Bank Berhad ("AmInvestment Bank"), part of AmBank Group Berhad, one of Malaysia's largest leading banking groups, today announced a partnership to expand the global investment opportunities available to AmInvestment Bank clients. Powered by GTN's co-branded global trading platform, GTN Trade, AmInvestment Bank will enable its clients seamless access to 13 global markets, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Singapore, Hong Kong, Japan, and Australia. Through a single integration, AmInvestment Bank can offer access to multiple markets without having to establish separate broker relationships or build the associated connectivity and post-trade infrastructure for each market. GTN Trade operates under AmInvestment Bank's brand, while GTN provides the underlying execution, custody and settlement infrastructure, enabling AmInvestment Bank to bring its global investing offering to market more efficiently. "At GTN, we believe access to global markets should be simpler and more accessible to investors," said Julien Le Noble, CEO Asia at GTN. "Our infrastructure enables financial institutions to expand their investment offerings and connect clients to global markets without having to build the underlying capabilities themselves. By partnering with AmInvestment Bank, we are helping bring global investing opportunities to more Malaysian investors through a familiar banking relationship." "Our goal is to make global investing simpler and more accessible for our clients. Through this partnership with GTN, we are enhancing our investment offering by providing convenient access to 13 global markets, enabling clients to diversify their portfolios and capture opportunities across different geographies and sectors. More importantly, this is a strategic step in strengthening our wealth and investment services, empowering Malaysian investors to look beyond domestic markets with greater choice and flexibility. By combining AmInvestment Bank's market expertise and established presence in Malaysia with GTN's global trading infrastructure, we are well positioned to deliver a more seamless and integrated investment experience that supports our clients' evolving financial needs and long-term investment aspirations," said Christopher Ng, Chief Executive Officer of AmInvestment Bank. The partnership reflects the growing importance of international market access as investors look beyond their domestic markets to diversify their portfolios. By combining AmInvestment Bank's established presence in Malaysia with GTN's global brokerage infrastructure, the partnership will make it easier for AmInvestment Bank clients to access investment opportunities across major global markets and the wider Southeast Asian region. About GTN GTN is the global fintech infrastructure powering limitless investment through a unified API-first architecture. By combining cloud-native technology with deep institutional expertise, GTN provides brokers, banks, asset managers, and fintechs with brokerage infrastructure spanning 90+ markets and up to 8 asset classes across GTN's six regulated entities, through a single API, enabling partners to create the next generation of investing and trading experiences. From fractional trading and micro-portfolios, including $1 fractional bonds, to full-service brokerage, GTN automates the investment lifecycle from digital onboarding to post-trade settlement. As a single counterparty, GTN reduces technical and regulatory burdens, enabling investment banks, brokerage firms, and wealth management firms to scale without having to build technology from scratch. GTN has over 700 professionals across 14 countries and serves more than 500 clients worldwide, united by one mission: transforming the accessibility of investment and trading opportunities. GTN operates through six regulated entities, each authorised in its own jurisdiction: FCA in the UK, DFSA in the DIFC, MAS in Singapore, SEC and FINRA in the US, FSCA in South Africa, and SFC in Hong Kong. Strategic investors include IFC (World Bank Group) and SBI Ventures Singapore. To learn more, visit www.gtngroup.com or follow us on LinkedIn.
